- When sentiment is consistently low (avg < 0.3) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to compensate for bearish bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overreacts and forecasts a prolonged overshoot; cap forecast at +3% above peak or reduce slope after 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (avg > 0.6) and model forecasts decline, reverse the trend direction by 1–2% in the first 3–5 days of forecast horizon.
- Mean reversion is overestimated in early forecast window; for days 1–7, apply a 0.5–1% downward bias if recent price is above 30-day moving average.
- When sentiment is volatile (±0.25 range over 3 days), model tends to over-smooth; add 0.5–1% noise to forecast for days 1–3 to reflect sentiment uncertainty.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows >10% deviation from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with 14-day trend, not 30-day trend.
